syndromes.syndrome: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis: psychiatric symptoms, memory/speech deficits, seizures, dyskinesias, decreased consciousness, autonomic instability, central hypoventilation

demographics: 95% younger than 45 y and 37% younger than 18 y; female:male ~4:1, less marked in children <12 and adults >45 (Graus 2016, citing Titulaer 2013)

tumors.frequencyText: Overall 38% (PNS-Care); 58% in women >18 y; 0–5% in children <12 y (Graus 2016)
Tumors in 23% of adults >45 y, usually carcinomas rather than teratomas (Graus 2016)

cancerScreening: Women: screen for ovarian teratoma (pelvic imaging per local protocol)
Adults >45 y: screen for carcinoma
Consider rescreening in relapsing or refractory disease (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: CSF positive in 250/250 vs serum 214/250 (sensitivity 100% vs 85.6%) on paired samples (Gresa-Arribas 2014)
Test both serum and CSF; CSF screening is obligatory for suspected surface-antibody encephalitis (PNS-Care 2021)
methodNotes: Surface antibody positive in serum only (CSF negative): confirm with tissue IHC or a research laboratory before calling it definite (PNS-Care 2021)
IgG against GluN1 is the relevant antibody (Graus 2016)

typicalFindings: Lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, or oligoclonal bands
Often normal or nonspecific; may show transient cortical/subcortical FLAIR changes

otherTests: EEG: abnormal in 90% (432/482) (Titulaer 2013); extreme delta brush supports the diagnosis (Graus 2016 criteria)
pearls: Good outcome (mRS 0–2) in 81% (203/252) at 24 months; recovery can continue for up to 18 months
Second-line immunotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide) is usually effective when first-line fails; early treatment and no ICU admission predict good outcome
Relapse risk 12% within 2 years; 67% of relapses milder than the first episode (Titulaer 2013)
Titers fall with recovery but often stay positive (24/28 CSF, 17/23 serum after recovery) — persistent positivity alone doesn't define activity
CSF titer change tracks relapse better than serum (14/19 vs 7/16); higher titers with teratoma or poor outcome (Gresa-Arribas 2014)

demographics: 66% male (25/38); median onset 64 y (range 31–84) (van Sonderen 2016)

tumors.frequencyText: 11% (4/36) in van Sonderen 2016, relation to LGI1 uncertain; <10%, mainly Morvan with LGI1 + CASPR2 (PNS-Care)

cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Serum positive in 38/38 by CBA and IHC; CSF positive in only 9/17 (53%) by CBA and 15/17 by IHC (van Sonderen 2016)
CSF-only positivity in 8% of paired samples (Ariño 2016) — send both, but never rely on CSF alone
methodNotes: Antibodies are IgG4 (Ariño 2016)

normalPercentText: Pleocytosis >5 cells/μL in 16% (5/32) and protein >0.58 g/L in 16% (5/32) (van Sonderen 2016)

Intrathecal IgG synthesis rare (Graus 2016)
Unilateral (60%) or bilateral (14%) hippocampal T2 lesions; mesial temporal sclerosis at follow-up in 7/16 (44%) with initial hippocampal lesions (text; Table 1 lists denominator 17)
Initial MRI can be normal with later limbic changes (Ariño 2016)

otherTests: Serum sodium: hyponatremia in 65% (24/37) (van Sonderen 2016)
EEG: epileptic activity 31%, focal slowing 25% (11/36, 9/36); FBDS have no EEG correlate
pearls: FBDS often precede memory loss — treating early is the window

Substantial response in 80%, but relapses in 35% (up to 8 y later); 86% have persistent amnesia for the illness, most survivors have mild residual cognitive deficit; 2-y case fatality 19% (van Sonderen 2016)

syndromes.syndrome: Cerebellar dysfunction, neuropathic pain, insomnia, dysautonomia, weight loss

demographics: 89% male (34/38); median onset 66 y; women younger (median 49 vs 68 y) (van Sonderen 2016)

tumors.frequencyText: 19% overall (van Sonderen 2016); ~50% malignant thymoma in Morvan syndrome, LE almost always nonparaneoplastic (PNS-Care)

cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)
Morvan syndrome: treated as intermediate risk by PNS-Care — screen for thymoma

rationale: Serum positive with both CBA and IHC in all 38 patients (van Sonderen 2016)
CSF IHC was negative in 3 patients, all with tumor and Morvan syndrome
methodNotes: IgG4 in all; IgG1 also in 63% (van Sonderen 2016)

typicalFindings: Mild pleocytosis (6–20 cells/μL) in 7 patients

normalPercentText: Unremarkable in 70% of patients with cognitive decline or seizures (van Sonderen 2016)
typicalFindings: Bilateral medial temporal T2 hyperintensity in 24%

otherTests: EMG/nerve conduction for peripheral nerve hyperexcitability
pearls: Seven core features: encephalopathy (cognitive/seizures), cerebellar dysfunction, peripheral nerve hyperexcitability, dysautonomia, insomnia, neuropathic pain, weight loss — ≥3 in 77%
Slow course: median time to nadir 4 months, >1 year in 30%
Treatment response 93%; relapses 25% (van Sonderen 2016)

demographics: Male:female 12:8; patients without SCLC younger (median 39 y) than those with SCLC (median 67.5 y) (Höftberger 2013)

Chest CT (± PET) for SCLC

rationale: Paired samples: CSF positive 12/12 vs serum 8/12 (Höftberger 2013)
Pooled: CSF 98.3% (71/72) vs serum 88.1% (69/77) (McKay 2019)
methodNotes: Surface antibody positive in serum only (CSF negative): confirm with tissue IHC or a research laboratory before calling it definite (PNS-Care 2021)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis + raised protein 7/19, pleocytosis only 6/19, protein only 1/19 (Höftberger 2013)

Hippocampal/amygdala FLAIR/T2 signal (LE pattern) 9/19; pial/cortical enhancement 2/19; leukoencephalopathy 1/19
Pooled: temporal T2 hyperintensity 54.8% (McKay 2019)

otherTests: EEG: abnormal in 9/15, epileptiform 6/15 (Höftberger 2013)
Onconeuronal antibody panel

Evaluate for myasthenia/thymoma

demographics: Median 57 y, 8/9 male (Hara 2017); median 53 y, 12/20 men (Tobin 2014)

GI evaluation for unexplained diarrhea/weight loss

syndromes.syndrome: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome: proximal leg-predominant weakness, autonomic dysfunction (~90%), reduced reflexes that improve after exercise

tumors.frequencyText: ~50% in LEMS; nearly 90% with rapidly progressive cerebellar syndrome (PNS-Care)

rationale: Present in nearly 90% of LEMS, similarly in paraneoplastic and nonparaneoplastic forms (PNS-Care)

SOX1 antibodies

syndromes.syndrome: Limbic, diencephalic, or brainstem encephalitis (95% over follow-up); classic LE alone only 26%
Excessive daytime sleepiness (32%), sometimes narcolepsy-cataplexy with low CSF hypocretin
Eye movement abnormalities with brainstem involvement

demographics: Young men → testicular tumors and isolated Ma2; older patients → lung cancer, often with Ma1 + Ma2 (PNS-Care; Dalmau 2004)
cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Men: testicular ultrasound (microcalcification and cryptorchidism were risk markers in 2 patients without cancer); chest CT
Neurologic symptoms preceded tumor diagnosis in 62% (Dalmau 2004)

rationale: Antibodies present in serum and in all 13 CSF samples available (Dalmau 2004)
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)
Additional Ma1 antibodies (15/38): more non-testicular tumors, ataxia, and worse prognosis

normalPercentText: Abnormal in 78% (25/32); normal cell count and protein in 7/32, 2 of whom had oligoclonal bands (Dalmau 2004)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 5–113 WBC/mm³ (median 20); protein 47–747 mg/dL (median 71)
CSF hypocretin can be low with hypersomnolence

normalPercentText: Abnormal in 74% overall; 89% with limbic or diencephalic dysfunction (Dalmau 2004)
typicalFindings: T2/FLAIR changes in medial temporal lobes, diencephalon/hypothalamus, or upper brainstem

otherTests: Endocrine panel (hypothalamic involvement)
Sleep study / CSF hypocretin if hypersomnolent
pearls: Better outcome with male sex, age <45, testicular tumor with complete response, no Ma1 antibodies, limited CNS involvement
Immunosuppression wasn't associated with improvement overall but clearly helped some (Dalmau 2004)
MRI can mimic a tumor — test for Ma2 before biopsy

cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: CSF positive with serum negative in 2/28 — send CSF (Bernal 2003)
methodNotes: DNER cell-based assay available (de Graaff 2012)

pearls: 22/28 had a subacute, irreversible severe cerebellar syndrome; 4 improved clearly
Age matters: complete remission in 3/7 aged ≤40 vs 1 partial remission among 21 older patients (Bernal 2003)

otherTests: Electrodiagnostic testing for LEMS
P/Q VGCC antibodies

demographics: All men; median 46 y (28–73) (Dubey 2020)

tumors.frequencyText: 80% (PNS-Care); of 36 screened: germ-cell tumor 64%, microlithiasis/fibrosis suggesting regressed tumor 19% (Dubey 2020)

cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Testicular ultrasound (look for microlithiasis/fibrosis as well as tumor); CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ± FDG-PET

rationale: PNS-Care recommends serum and CSF
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)

Can look like a mass lesion → misdiagnosed as tumor/metastasis
Follow-up >2 y: cerebellar atrophy 6/12; hypertrophic olivary degeneration 3

rationale: Cohort defined mainly by serum (92 of 96 archived specimens) (Gadoth 2017)
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC with confirmatory testing (PNS-Care)
Often accompanied by other SCLC markers: CRMP5 26%, VGCC 22%, Hu 13% (Gadoth 2017)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis in 15/29 (52%, median 20 cells); raised protein in 21/29 (74%, median 60 mg/dL) (Gadoth 2017)

normalPercentText: Brain/spine MRI normal in 15/43 (35%); nonspecific white-matter change in 8 more (Gadoth 2017)
typicalFindings: Pathologic in 46%: spinal cord T2 lesions/enhancement, cerebral atrophy, optic nerve or temporal lobe involvement, meningeal enhancement

Nerve conduction studies

Acute brainstem, diencephalic (symptomatic narcolepsy), or cerebral syndromes

demographics: Female > male; pediatric onset extremely rare (Banwell 2023 Table 1)

cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Diagnosis rests on positive serum AQP4-IgG by cell-based assay plus ≥1 core clinical characteristic (Wingerchuk 2015)
methodNotes: Cell-based assay recommended (Wingerchuk 2015)

typicalFindings: CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands infrequent (5–20%) vs >80% in MS (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
Pleocytosis can be marked
Brain MRI might be normal with optic neuritis or myelitis presentations (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
Lesions in AQP4-rich regions: peri-third/fourth ventricle, splenium, internal capsule, dorsal medulla; patchy cloud-like or pencil-thin ependymal enhancement
Spinal cord: bright spotty lesions; residual T1-hypointense lesions might be present (21–50%)
Banwell 2023 Table 1 frequency bands: infrequent 5–20%, might be present 21–50%

otherTests: MOG-IgG if AQP4 negative
MRI orbits and whole spine with contrast
pearls: Risk of poor visual recovery and of worsening motor impairment with relapses (Banwell 2023 Table 1) — treat attacks urgently
Interferon-beta, natalizumab, and fingolimod can worsen NMOSD

Myelitis — longitudinally extensive or multiple; gray-matter H-sign; conus lesions
Cerebral cortical encephalitis with seizures; brainstem/cerebellar syndromes

demographics: Female = male; pediatric onset frequent (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Serum is the preferred specimen; CSF positivity in seropositive MOGAD ranged 42–61% in cited series (Banwell 2023)
CSF-only positives occur rarely and can support MOGAD in seronegative patients with supportive clinical/MRI features
methodNotes: Live cell-based assay preferred; fixed CBA acceptable; ELISA not recommended (Banwell 2023)
Fixed CBA: clear positive ≥1:100; low positive 1:10 to <1:100 — low positives need AQP4-IgG negativity plus ≥1 supporting clinical or MRI feature
Test before steroids/IVIG/PLEX when possible; if negative but suspicion high, repeat ≥3 months later or at relapse
Titers usually fall over time but can stay positive for years

typicalFindings: CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands infrequent (5–20%) vs >80% in MS (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
Brain MRI might be normal with optic neuritis or myelitis presentations
Fluffy, poorly demarcated T2 lesions in white matter, deep gray matter, middle cerebellar peduncle; partial or complete resolution expected; T1-hypointense residua extremely rare (<5%)
Leptomeningeal enhancement around brainstem; unilateral/bilateral cortical leptomeningeal enhancement with cortical encephalitis
Banwell 2023 Table 1 frequency bands: infrequent 5–20%, might be present 21–50%

otherTests: AQP4-IgG (negative result needed to interpret low-positive MOG)
Fundoscopy / OCT
pearls: Course monophasic or relapsing; recovery after attacks typically favorable (vision, motor), though residual sphincter/erectile dysfunction can follow myelitis (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
False positives more likely with low titers — don't diagnose MOGAD from a low positive in an MS-like picture

syndromes.syndrome: Meningoencephalomyelitis — meningitis, encephalitis, myelitis, or combinations (81%)

demographics: Median onset 44 y (8–103); 54% women (Flanagan 2017)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)
Pelvic imaging for ovarian teratoma — predicted best when NMDAR-IgG and AQP4-IgG coexist (71%) (Flanagan 2017)

rationale: Paired samples: CSF positive 45/49 (92%) vs serum 22/49 (45%); CSF testing had the highest specificity for meningoencephalomyelitis (94%) (Flanagan 2017)
methodNotes: GFAPα-IgG is the most sensitive isoform (100%)
Rare false positives in controls: serum tissue assay 0.5%, serum CBA 1.5%, CSF CBA 0.9% — serum-only positives are less specific

typicalFindings: Median 78.5 cells (13–550), lymphocyte-predominant; protein raised in 30/36 (median 80 mg/dL); low glucose in 4/22; CSF-restricted OCB in 13/24
Linear perivascular radial enhancement extending from the ventricles in 53%; also leptomeningeal (22%), serpentine (19%), ependymal (9%)
Spinal cord: longitudinally extensive lesions common; central canal enhancement in 21%
DWI normal in all evaluated; lesions often resolve with steroids

otherTests: NMDAR-IgG and AQP4-IgG (coexist; affect tumor risk)
Vessel imaging if vasculitis is suspected — angiography was normal in all tested
pearls: Improved with corticosteroids in 14/16 — but relapses during taper (often below prednisone 20 mg/day) or after stopping steroid-sparing therapy; plan steroid-sparing maintenance (Flanagan 2017)
Mimics CNS vasculitis on imaging (32% considered) — angiography was uniformly negative

entries.antigen: Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor type 1 (ITPR1; endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ channel)

syndromes.syndrome: Subacute cerebellar ataxia (Purkinje cell 'Medusa head' antibody)
Peripheral sensorimotor (radiculo)neuropathy, GBS-like or slowly progressive
Encephalitis/encephalopathy with seizures or cognitive decline
Other: dysautonomia (incl. pandysautonomia), sleep disorder, dystonia, spastic paraparesis

demographics: Median onset 64 y (range 13–83); M:F 1:1.5 (Jarius 2022, pooled n=21)
Mayo series: median 64 y (range 7–83); 10/14 female; 2 pediatric (Alfugham 2018)
Peripheral phenotype median 60 y vs CNS phenotype 65 y (Jarius 2022)
cancerScreening: Cancer in 9/20 (45%) with data (Jarius 2022); 5/14 (36%) in Mayo series (Alfugham 2018); both advise thorough tumor search in every seropositive pt
Modalities used in Mayo series: FDG-PET/CT, mammography (Alfugham 2018)
Tumor often already disseminated: metastases at presentation in 5/7 solid tumors (Jarius 2022)
Late tumor possible: breast cancer 11 y after ataxia onset (onset age 28) in 1 pt (Berzero 2017)
PNS-Care rescreening (every 4–6 mo for 2 y) is specified only for high-risk antibodies with high-risk phenotypes; ITPR1 is not tiered (Graus 2021)

rationale: Serum CBA positive in all seropositive pts analysed; median serum CBA titer 1:30,720 (range 1:320–1:245,760; n=13) (Jarius 2022)
CSF IgG mainly extrathecal: CSF/serum ratio median 0.017; antibody index <4 in 2/2 tested (Jarius 2022)
CSF-only positive reports exist (5 excluded from pooled review) (Jarius 2022); PNS-Care advises testing serum and CSF (Graus 2021)
methodNotes: Tissue IHC/IFA: Purkinje somata, dendrites, axons ('Medusa head'), nearly identical to anti-Ca/ARHGAP26; ITPR1 CBA distinguishes (Jarius 2014)
Commercial CBA (Euroimmun); Mayo screening dilution serum 1:10, CSF 1:2 (Alfugham 2018)
Specificity: absent in 250 healthy and 105 non-neurological controls (Jarius 2022)
IgG2-only in milder cases (3 pts); IgG1-predominant in 2 pts with more severe outcome (Jarius 2022)
Coexisting neural IgGs reported: low-titer GAD65; CSF NMDAR + GFAP in 1 (Alfugham 2018)

typicalFindings: Pooled seropositive pts: elevated protein 4/7, pleocytosis 1/5, OCB negative 5/6 (Jarius 2022)
Mayo series: elevated protein and pleocytosis in 4/5 tested (Alfugham 2018); conflicts with pooled data (see verify)
Acellular CSF with normal protein and no OCB in the MSA-C-like case (Berzero 2017)
Ataxia: cerebellar or pontocerebellar atrophy (Alfugham 2018; Jarius 2022)
Pontocerebellar atrophy with hot cross bun sign in 1 pt, MSA-C mimic (Berzero 2017)
Myelopathy: posterior column T2 change or longitudinally extensive myelitis; nerve-root enhancement (Alfugham 2018)
Encephalitis: mesial temporal or cortical-subcortical T2 lesions ± enhancement; temporal-predominant atrophy (Alfugham 2018)

otherTests: EMG/NCS: mixed sensorimotor radiculopolyneuropathy, delayed F waves, no conduction block (Jarius 2016); axonal or demyelinating neuropathy (Alfugham 2018)
Autonomic testing (TST/ART) abnormal in pandysautonomia with normal EMG (Alfugham 2018)
EEG: status epilepticus in 1, electrographic seizures in 1 (Jarius 2022)
FDG-PET: medial temporal/striatal hypermetabolism with normal MRI (Jarius 2022); increased cerebellar uptake with normal MRI in 1 ataxia pt (Alfugham 2018)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); pooled cancer rate 9/20 (45%), which the authors note would fit the PNS-Care intermediate-risk range (30–70%) (Jarius 2022)
No significant improvement in any of 10 immunotherapy-treated Mayo pts (Alfugham 2018); clear benefit only in isolated cases (Jarius 2022)
Neuropathy is the most cancer-associated phenotype: cancer in 3/5 with neuropathy (Alfugham 2018)
Rare: 0.015% of 52,000 specimens over 12 mo (Alfugham 2018)
Germline ITPR1 mutations cause SCA15/SCA29, a distinct genetic differential (Jarius 2014)

entries.antigen: Adaptor protein-3 complex subunit beta-2 (AP3B2; beta-neuronal adaptin-like protein, synaptic vesicle coat)

syndromes.syndrome: Subacute rapidly progressive gait ataxia: cerebellar or spinocerebellar
Myeloneuropathy (dorsal column tractopathy ± longitudinally extensive cord lesion)

demographics: Median onset 42 y (range 24–58); 6/10 female (Honorat 2019)
Published cases span 10–73 y; 9/14 female (Liu 2025 Table 1)
Pediatric cases reported: 10 y (Liu 2025 Table 1) and 15 y (Garza 2021)

tumors.frequencyText: 1/9, found prospectively; AP3B2 not detected in tumor sections (Honorat 2019)

cancerScreening: Cancer in 2/9: RCC at presentation 1, remote B-cell lymphoma 1; both pts died (Honorat 2019)
PNS-Care rescreening (every 4–6 mo for 2 y) is specified only for high-risk antibodies; AP3B2 is not tiered (Graus 2021)

rationale: IFA positive in serum of 10/10 pts and in all 6 CSF specimens (Honorat 2019)
Serum IFA endpoint median 1:30,720 (range 3,840–61,440); CSF median 1:64 (range 32–256) (Honorat 2019)
CSF CBA positive in 3/3 tested (Honorat 2019)
methodNotes: Tissue IFA: synaptic pattern resembling amphiphysin-IgG; Purkinje perikarya, cerebellar granular-layer synapses, dentate, spinal dorsal horn, DRG and sympathetic ganglia (Honorat 2019)
Series found among specimens archived as 'amphiphysin-like' synaptic staining (Honorat 2019)
Western blot alone not specific: 1/50 control sera WB-positive but IFA- and CBA-negative; all 470 IFA controls negative (Honorat 2019)
Confirm by CBA (Euroimmun biochip, AP3B2 isoform 1) (Honorat 2019)
No binding to live hippocampal neurons, consistent with intracellular target (Honorat 2019)
Coexisting low-level N-type VGCC IgG in 8/10 (median 0.07 nmol/L) and low-titer GAD65 in 2 (Honorat 2019)

typicalFindings: WBC elevated 4/6 (median 7/µL, range 6–8); protein elevated 3/6 (median 46 mg/dL, range 39–87); CSF-exclusive OCB 2/6; raised IgG index/synthesis 1/6 (Honorat 2019)

normalPercentText: Brain MRI normal in 3/10 and spinal cord MRI normal in 3/7 of published cases with imaging (Liu 2025 Table 1)
typicalFindings: Cerebellar (vermis-predominant) atrophy in 4/4 with cerebellar ataxia (Honorat 2019)
Cord MRI abnormal in 3/6 imaged, all with myeloneuropathy: posterior-column LETM/tractopathy, central gray T2 signal, cord atrophy (Honorat 2019)
Bilateral subcortical/periventricular white-matter T2 lesions in 1 (Honorat 2019)
Hemicerebellar atrophy with focal T2 lesion in 1 pediatric case (Garza 2021)

otherTests: EMG abnormal in 4: diffuse large-fiber sensory neuropathy 2, sensory neuronopathy 1, severe thoracic/lumbosacral polyradiculopathy 1 (Honorat 2019)
Sural nerve biopsy (1): endoneurial CD68+ macrophages, multifocal large- and small-fiber loss, consistent with neuron-directed cytotoxicity (Honorat 2019)
B12 and copper/ceruloplasmin normal in all Mayo-evaluated pts (Honorat 2019)
Early sensory involvement may be asymmetric (neuronopathy/mononeuropathy multiplex pattern) before becoming symmetric (Liu 2025)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); cancer in 2/9 (Honorat 2019)
Gait disturbance unifies the syndrome: all 9 with data; sensory ataxia in 5, cerebellar ataxia in 4 (Honorat 2019)
Immunotherapy: 0/5 improved, but none worsened over median 36 mo follow-up (range 3–94) (Honorat 2019); mild improvement in 2/8 treated in pooled literature (Liu 2025)
Mixed signs: 2 cerebellar pts had leg areflexia with bilateral Babinski (Honorat 2019)
Coexisting systemic autoimmunity: Sjögren, systemic sclerosis, hypothyroidism (1 each) (Honorat 2019)
Consider in B12-refractory SCD-like myeloneuropathy with normal B12 and copper (Liu 2025)
Lab report may first read 'unclassified synaptic / amphiphysin-like' IFA pattern (Honorat 2019)

entries.antigen: Septin-5 (CDCrel-1; presynaptic GTP-binding protein regulating neurotransmitter exocytosis)

syndromes.syndrome: Subacute rapidly progressive (pan)cerebellar ataxia with prominent hyperkinetic eye movement disorder, oscillopsia, vertigo
Eye movement disorder with truncal/limb myoclonus, later encephalopathy
Psychiatric features (apathy, emotional blunting) with coexisting septin-7-IgG

demographics: Septin-5 cohort (n=8): 6 M, 2 F; age 40–70 y, median 59.5 (Hinson 2022 Table S1)
Index series: median onset 59 y (range 47–62) (Honorat 2018)
cancerScreening: No neoplasm in 8/8 septin-5-IgG pts (Hinson 2022)
Septin-5 is expressed in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, but no paraneoplastic case reported (Honorat 2018)
PNS-Care rescreening rule applies only to high-risk antibodies; septin-5 is not tiered (Graus 2021)

rationale: Septin IFA pattern in all 12 CSF and 17/18 sera; 1 pt positive in CSF only (Hinson 2022)
Median titers (septin-5 + -7 cohort): CSF 1:256 (range 4–2048), serum 1:15,360 (range 480–61,440) (Hinson 2022)
Septin-5 index series: serum median 1:15,360 (range 7,680–15,360); intrathecal vs systemic origin unknown (Honorat 2018)
methodNotes: Tissue IFA 'septin pattern': diffuse synaptic (neuropil) staining, cerebellar molecular layer and thalamus strongest, plus myenteric plexus and renal glomeruli (Hinson 2022)
Extra gastric mucosal and renal interstitial staining indicates septin-7-IgG; septin-5 vs -7 resolved by CBA (Euroimmun, isoform 1) (Hinson 2022)
Reactive with septin-5 isoform 1 only; all controls negative by IFA and CBA (Honorat 2018)
Coexisting septin-6/-11 IgG by WB in 1/4 tested (Hinson 2022); septin-4 IgG in 1 (Honorat 2018)
Coexisting N-type VGCC IgG in 2 and GAD65 in 2 (0.17 and 28.1 nmol/L) (Honorat 2018)
Patient IgG binds live hippocampal neuron surfaces, colocalizing with synaptophysin (Hinson 2022)

normalPercentText: No abnormal value reported in 1/5 with CSF data (20%) (Hinson 2022 Table S1)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 3/5 (8, 35, 144/µL, lymphocytic); protein elevated 3/5 (47–115 mg/dL); raised IgG synthesis rate 2/5; CSF-exclusive OCB (14) in 1 (Hinson 2022 Table S1)

normalPercentText: Normal in 4/7 septin-5 pts with imaging (57%) (Hinson 2022)
typicalFindings: Focal cerebellar (vermis) atrophy in 2/7 (Hinson 2022), early in course in 1 (Honorat 2018)
Diffuse cerebellar T2 hyperintensity with FDG hypermetabolism in 1 (Hinson 2022 Table S1)

otherTests: FDG-PET: focal cerebellar hypermetabolism in 1/7 septin-5 pts (Hinson 2022)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); no neoplasm in 8/8 (Hinson 2022)
All 8 septin-5 pts had pancerebellar ataxia; 7/8 prominent eye movement disorders (Hinson 2022)
Vestibular mimic: 1 pt first diagnosed as labyrinthitis (vertigo, intractable nausea/vomiting before ataxia) (Honorat 2018)
Outcomes: improvement in 4/5 treated, often partial or relapsing on steroid taper (rituximab or cyclophosphamide used); 1 spontaneous recovery; 1 treated pt died (Hinson 2022 Table S1)
Eye findings recorded: downbeat plus periodic alternating nystagmus (1), diplopia (2) (Hinson 2022 Table S1)
Coexisting GRAF1-IgG in 1 (Hinson 2022 Table S1)
Septin-5 is enriched in cerebellar dentate nuclei, matching the oculomotor phenotype (Hinson 2022)
Coexisting septin-7-IgG in 2/8; 1 developed apathy, emotional blunting, poor insight (Hinson 2022)
Onset 1 mo after SARS-CoV-2 illness in 1 (Hinson 2022)
Very rare: septin pattern in 0.003% of sera and 0.004% of CSF screened (Hinson 2022)

entries.antigen: Neurochondrin (NCDN, norbin; intracellular somatodendritic protein interacting with mGluR1/mGluR5)

syndromes.syndrome: Rapidly progressive rhombencephalitis: cerebellar ataxia with brainstem signs (eye movement abnormality, dysphagia, vomiting)
Subacute-to-chronic cerebellar ataxia (primary autoimmune cerebellar ataxia)
Pediatric chorea, dystonia, recurrent ataxia or encephalopathy

demographics: Mayo series: median onset 43 y (range 30–69); 5/8 female (Shelly 2019)
Pooled literature (n=19): 12 M, 7 F; age 2.6–69 y; 6 pediatric (<16 y) (Schwarzwald 2023)

tumors.frequencyText: 1/7 Mayo pts (Shelly 2019); the only cancer among 19 published cases (Schwarzwald 2023)

cancerScreening: Cancer rare: 1/19 published cases (Schwarzwald 2023)
Whole-body FDG-PET/CT plus gynecologic/urologic exams repeated over 2–10 y found no tumor in 3 pts (Miske 2017)
PNS-Care rescreening rule applies only to high-risk antibodies; neurochondrin is not tiered (Graus 2021)

rationale: Index Mayo series detected in 8 serum and 4 CSF specimens from 8 pts (Shelly 2019)
Median titers: serum 1:30,720 (range 3,840–61,440); CSF 1:64 (range 2–256) (Shelly 2019)
Intrathecal synthesis (antibody index ≥4) in 2/3 (Miske 2017)
methodNotes: Tissue IFA: synaptic/cytoplasmic pattern strongest in hippocampus (stratum lucidum, CA2/CA3, dentate), cerebellar Purkinje cytoplasm and molecular layer, amygdala (Shelly 2019)
CBA alone not specific: positive in 2/196 healthy controls whose tissue IFA was negative (Shelly 2019); confirm with tissue IFA
Antigen confirmed by ~75 kDa immunoblot band and recombinant western blot (Shelly 2019)
IgG1 subclass; titers largely unchanged during immunosuppression (Miske 2017)

normalPercentText: Normal in 2/16 with data (13%) (Schwarzwald 2023); abnormal in 5/5 Mayo pts (Shelly 2019)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 11/16 and OCB 11/16 in pooled cases (Schwarzwald 2023)
Mayo series: lymphocytic pleocytosis 3/3 tested (14–185/µL, median 18); elevated protein 5/5; CSF-exclusive OCB 3/3; raised IgG index 3/3 (Shelly 2019)
Cerebellar (often vermian) atrophy in 10/18 (Schwarzwald 2023); severe cerebellar atrophy at last follow-up in 5/7 Mayo pts (Shelly 2019)
Early MRI may be normal: 2/7 normal at onset (Shelly 2019); normal initial MRI then 29% cerebellar volume loss over 2 y (Schwarzwald 2023)
Early T2 lesions in cerebellum/brainstem, rhombencephalon-restricted enhancement, hippocampal or striatal T2 change; longitudinally extensive cord T2 lesion in 1 (Shelly 2019)
Supratentorial cortical gray-matter atrophy with DTI white-matter changes (Miske 2017)

otherTests: Quantitative cerebellar volumetry documented progressive volume loss in 1 (Schwarzwald 2023)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); cancer in 1/19 published cases (Schwarzwald 2023)
Mayo adults: poor outcome despite early treatment: 5/6 treated within 1 mo of onset, but only 1 remained ambulatory; 1 died (Shelly 2019)
Pooled outcomes (n=19): at least slight improvement 10, stable 4, progressed 4, died 1 (Schwarzwald 2023)
Cyclophosphamide was followed by improvement or stabilization in 4/5; 3/4 adults given B-cell depletion progressed (Schwarzwald 2023; small numbers)
Children may present with chorea minor (Rommel 2017), dystonia or encephalopathy (Schwarzwald 2023)
Coexisting systemic autoimmunity: Sjögren syndrome, thyroiditis (1 each) (Shelly 2019)
Rare: 8 pts among 616,025 specimens screened 1993–2018 (Shelly 2019)

entries.antigen: Tripartite motif-containing protein 46 (TRIM46; axon initial segment microtubule-binding protein)

syndromes.syndrome: Subacute cerebellar syndrome, isolated or with encephalopathy, brainstem signs, myelopathy or parkinsonism

demographics: Median age 67 y (range 25–87); 15/22 female (68%) (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Initial 3 pts: median 73 y (range 64–78), 1/3 female (Valencia-Sanchez 2022 suppl Table 2; van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)
cancerScreening: Cancer in 18/22 (82%); metastatic in 8 (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Cancer usually already known: diagnosed before neuro onset in 12/18 (median 17 mo prior, range 3 mo–8 y); found during neuro work-up in 6 (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Neuroendocrine lineage in half of cancers (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Late detection possible: SCLC 4 y after neuro onset in 1; 2 more with suspicious chest CT without histology (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
SCLC diagnosed 10 mo after ataxia onset in 1 initial pt (van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)
Authors argue TRIM46 should qualify as high-risk (>70% cancer) (Valencia-Sanchez 2022); not tiered in PNS-Care, so its 2-y rescreening rule is not formally specified (Graus 2021)

rationale: 25 seropositive pts: 9 serum only, 8 CSF only, 8 both (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
All 33 positive specimens confirmed by TRIM46 CBA (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
methodNotes: Tissue IFA: distinctive axon initial segment staining in cerebellar Purkinje layer, cerebral cortex, hippocampus; kidney and gastric mucosa non-reactive (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Confirm by CBA (transfected COS7 or HeLa) or western blot; patient IgG does not bind live-neuron surfaces (Valencia-Sanchez 2022; van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)
Specificity: negative in 69 SCLC and 10 Merkel cell carcinoma sera without neurological disease, and in autoimmune and healthy controls (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
208 healthy and disease controls (incl. 80 SCLC pts with or without Hu-IgG) were CBA-negative (van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)
Polyclonal response to multiple TRIM46 epitopes (Valencia-Sanchez 2022; van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)

typicalFindings: Inflammatory (elevated WBC or CSF-restricted supernumerary OCB) in 9/14 (64%) (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Post-ICI case: no pleocytosis, protein 67 mg/dL, 6 CSF-unique OCB, IgG index 1.27 (Garza 2021)
Initial 3 pts: pleocytosis 14 and 25/µL in 2, normal in 1 (van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)
Cerebellar atrophy in 5/16; 1 also with medullary and pulvinar T2 hyperintensity (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Medial temporal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in 3/16 (bilateral 2) (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Post-ICI case: small medullary T2 lesion, then bilateral medullary and thalamic T2 change and cerebellar atrophy within 3 mo (Garza 2021)
Bilateral T2/DWI hyperintensity of caudate head, pallidum, hippocampus and cingulate in the CJD-like case (van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)

otherTests: EEG: progressive diffuse slowing in the CJD-like case; CSF 14-3-3 positive (van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); cancer in 18/22 (82%) (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
No significant improvement in any of 12 immunotherapy-treated pts with follow-up; 8 of them died (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Post-ICI: 3 pts, onset 2–8 mo after starting ICI; 2/3 partially improved after stopping ICI plus aggressive immunotherapy (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
CJD mimic: rapidly progressive dementia with myoclonus, basal ganglia/hippocampal DWI change and positive 14-3-3; autopsy showed CD8+ T-cell infiltrates (van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)
Female predominance (68%) despite the SCLC link: many tumors are gynecologic, breast or pancreatic (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
Authors recommend testing in intermediate- or high-risk PNS phenotypes, especially subacute cerebellar ataxia (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
TRIM46 is CNS-restricted, matching CNS-only phenotypes (Valencia-Sanchez 2022)
SIADH (Na 120 mmol/L) in 1 with encephalomyelitis and SCLC (van Coevorden-Hameete 2017)

Cognitive impairment, depression, pseudobulbar affect or psychosis
Parkinsonism (static) or long-tract signs with ataxia

demographics: Mayo series: median onset 51 y (range 14–76); about half male (Pittock 2020)
Previously published cases (n=10): age 24–84 y (Pittock 2020 Table 2)

tumors.tumor: Squamous cell carcinoma, head and neck (nasopharynx, lingual tonsil)
Other: ovarian, breast, melanoma, B-cell lymphoma, prostate, gastric adenocarcinoma
tumors.frequencyText: 1 each; tumor in half of 10 previously published cases (Pittock 2020)

cancerScreening: Evidence of cancer in 4 Mayo pts (33%); history of malignancy in 10/24 published cases (Pittock 2020)
Authors recommend searching for head and neck (nasopharynx) and lung tumors, ideally whole-body FDG-PET/CT, which found malignancy in 4 pts with negative conventional CT (Pittock 2020)
Ataxia can herald cancer: ovarian cancer found after anti-Ca detection (Jarius 2013)
PNS-Care rescreening rule applies only to high-risk antibodies; GRAF1 is not tiered (Graus 2021)

rationale: Confirmed in 11 sera and 6 CSF specimens from 17 pts (Pittock 2020)
IFA end-point titers: serum 1:7,680–1:61,440; CSF 1:64–1:1,024 (Pittock 2020)
methodNotes: Seropositivity requires both tissue IFA and CBA: 1 control was CBA-positive only (Pittock 2020)
CBA-only positives are common: 14 CBA-positive pts, only 3 also IHC-positive (Bartels 2018)
IFA 'Medusa head' pattern: Purkinje dendritic arbors in the molecular layer plus myenteric ganglia; hippocampus not stained (Pittock 2020)
Only 17 of 119 Medusa-head-like patterns were GRAF1 by CBA; look-alikes stain hippocampus brightly (Pittock 2020)
ITPR1-IgG gives a near-identical Purkinje pattern but does not bind ARHGAP26; CBA separates them (Jarius 2014)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 5/7, supernumerary OCB 3/7, raised IgG index 1/7 (Pittock 2020)
Cerebellar atrophy 5/11; brainstem atrophy 2; cerebral atrophy 2 (Pittock 2020)
Across published cases: cerebellar atrophy in 8/18 with MRI (44%) (Pittock 2020)

otherTests: Autonomic neuropathy with severe gastroparesis in 1 (Pittock 2020)
Autonomic reflex testing normal in the pt with parkinsonism, arguing against MSA-C (Pittock 2020)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); cancer in about one-third of Mayo pts (Pittock 2020)
Ataxia progressive despite immunotherapy in all but 1, who stabilized; wheelchair dependence in all but 1 (Pittock 2020)
Ataxia in 20/24 (83%) of all published cases; neurocognitive features in 9 (Pittock 2020)
Peripheral somatic or autonomic neuropathy in close to one-third (Pittock 2020)
Index anti-Ca pt developed ataxia after a respiratory infection, with no cancer at 52 mo (Jarius 2013)
Very rare: 0.004% of sera (2/52,000) over 12 mo (Pittock 2020)
Can coexist with septin-5/-7-IgG (1 pt) (Hinson 2022 Table S1)

Prominent psychiatric features (depression, anxiety, behavioral change, psychosis)

demographics: Pooled n=26: 20/26 male (76.9%); median age 66 y (range 48–94) (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Original Lyon series: median 64 y (range 57–80) (Do 2017)
Mayo series: all 6 female; median 72 y (range 49–80) (McKeon-Makki 2022)
cancerScreening: No cancer and no autoimmune comorbidity in 26 reported pts (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021); no associated cancer in original 10 (Do 2017)

rationale: CSF more sensitive: tissue IFA pattern seen only in CSF; serum IFA negative in 3/3 tested, though serum CBA positive 3/3 (McKeon-Makki 2022)

normalPercentText: CSF abnormal in all reported pts (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 18/25 (72%); oligoclonal bands 18/25 (72%) (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Elevated tau 11/14 (78.6%) (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021), with normal Aβ42 and phospho-tau (Do 2017)
Mayo series: lymphocytic pleocytosis and supernumerary OCB in all 3 with data (McKeon-Makki 2022)

normalPercentText: No temporal FLAIR abnormality on initial MRI in 3/26 (12%) (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
typicalFindings: Temporal lobe FLAIR hyperintensity at onset 23/26 (88.5%); gadolinium enhancement 6/26 (23.1%); temporal enlargement possible (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Evolves to severe hippocampal atrophy in 17/19 (89.5%) (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Initial MRI normal, FLAIR change on repeat, in 1/10 (Do 2017); gadolinium enhancement on initial MRI in all 3 Mayo pts (McKeon-Makki 2022)

otherTests: EEG: epileptiform abnormalities in 2/17, without discharges (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
HLA: DRB1*03:01-DQA1*05:01-DQB1*02:01 in 8/11 (OR 14.4) (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Brain biopsy: CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltrates with granzyme B (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021); small-vessel CNS vasculitis in 1 (Vicino 2021)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); non-paraneoplastic in all reported pts (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Only 5/25 (20%) responded to immunotherapy, mostly mildly; outcome worse 8, stable 12, mild improvement 4, major improvement 1 (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Unlike LGI1/CASPR2 limbic encephalitis: no seizures at onset (0/25) and often a constitutional prodrome (weight loss, asthenia, anorexia 11/25) (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Depression in 17/25 (68%); anosmia/dysgeusia 4/25; prosopagnosia 6/25 (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Olfactory prodrome: burning-smell phantosmia for 6 mo before amnesia, without EEG correlate, in 1 (McKeon-Makki 2022)
Neurodegenerative/prion mimic: high CSF tau with normal Aβ42/phospho-tau (Do 2017), yet MRI and CSF are inflammatory (Muñiz-Castrillo 2021)
Consider in older adults with subacute anterograde amnesia (Do 2017)
Mayo series: all 3 treated (IVMP + IVIg, ~4 mo after onset) still needed help with daily living at last follow-up (McKeon-Makki 2022)

entries.antigen: Phosphodiesterase 10A (PDE10A; striatum-enriched cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase, membrane-bound and cytosolic isoforms)

syndromes.syndrome: Hyperkinetic movement disorder: chorea, hemiballismus, dystonia, dyskinesia
Encephalopathy (confusion), with or without movement disorder

demographics: Median age 70 y (range 66–76); 4/7 male (Zekeridou 2019)
4 further cases: median 61 y (range 53–68), 3 female (Valencia-Sanchez 2022 abstract)

tumors.tumor: Non-small-cell lung carcinoma (adenocarcinoma, squamous, poorly differentiated)

cancerScreening: Carcinoma confirmed in 6/7; the 7th had a lung nodule (Zekeridou 2019); cancer in 3/4 further cases (Valencia-Sanchez 2022 abstract)
Cancers often metastatic at neuro presentation (renal, pancreatic, with leptomeningeal spread in 2) (Zekeridou 2019)
PNS-Care rescreening rule applies only to high-risk antibodies; PDE10A is not tiered (Graus 2021)

rationale: Positive specimens: sera 7, CSF 4 from 7 pts; 1 pt identified from CSF only (Zekeridou 2019)
Serum IFA titers 1:15,360 to >1:30,720; CSF 1:4–1:64 (Zekeridou 2019)
methodNotes: Tissue IFA: basal ganglia-predominant synaptic staining, less in hippocampus, faint cerebellar granular layer; no similar pattern in >400,000 clinical samples (Zekeridou 2019)
Confirm with recombinant western blot and CBA (PDE10A1 and PDE10A2 isoforms) (Zekeridou 2019)
CBA-only faint positive in 1 control (renal carcinoma + AQP4-NMOSD) with negative IFA and WB: treat isolated low CBA results cautiously (Zekeridou 2019)
Negative in 26 ICI-treated cancer controls and 10 Huntington disease pts (Zekeridou 2019)

typicalFindings: Both ICI-associated cases: WBC ≤5/µL, protein 44–56 mg/dL, 8 and 14 CSF-restricted OCB (Zekeridou 2019)
Inflammatory CSF in 2/4 further cases (pleocytosis 1, CSF-unique OCB 1) (Valencia-Sanchez 2022 abstract)
Non-enhancing FLAIR/T2 basal ganglia hyperintensities in both hyperkinetic ICI cases, mirroring the IFA pattern (Zekeridou 2019)
Leptomeningeal enhancement in 2 with probable carcinomatous meningitis (Zekeridou 2019)

pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); carcinoma in 6/7 (Zekeridou 2019)
ICI trigger: hyperkinetic disorder began 4–5 mo after starting PD-1 inhibitor in 2/7 (Zekeridou 2019); hemichorea after ICI in 1 further case (Valencia-Sanchez 2022 abstract)
Immunotherapy: transient improvement with IV steroids in 1 of 2 treated (Zekeridou 2019); partial steroid response in 2 further cases (Valencia-Sanchez 2022 abstract)
Sustained symptom control in 1 came from tetrabenazine plus botulinum toxin (Zekeridou 2019)
High early mortality: 4/7 died shortly after neuro onset, mostly cancer-related (Zekeridou 2019)
Phenotype parallels genetic PDE10A disorders (hyperkinesia, bilateral striatal lesions); Huntington disease pts were seronegative (Zekeridou 2019)

entries.antigen: Dachshund homolog 1 (DACH1; nuclear transcription factor), the ANNA-3 antigen

syndromes.syndrome: Dysautonomia, incl. GI dysmotility and esophageal spasm
Ocular: chorioretinopathy, optic neuropathy, Adie pupil
Onset or worsening during immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy

demographics: Median age 63.5 y (range 49–88); 20/30 female (Zekeridou 2022)

tumors.frequencyText: 9/22 histologically confirmed cancers (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table); 5/7 biopsied tumors (Chan 2001)
14/22 (64%) histologically confirmed cancers, incl. SCLC, Merkel cell, gastric neuroendocrine, bladder small-cell and metastatic neuroendocrine of unknown primary (Zekeridou 2022 and suppl table)

tumors.tumor: Other: carcinomas of colon, breast, lung (non-small-cell), ovary; carcinoma of unknown primary; ovarian teratoma
tumors.frequencyText: Remainder of 22 confirmed; >1 malignancy in 4 pts (Zekeridou 2022)

cancerScreening: Cancer evident in 27/30 (90%) vs 15/100 general paraneoplastic-panel pts: 22 histologic, 4 lung mass ± hilar nodes, 1 FDG-avid mass (Zekeridou 2022)
Original series: intrathoracic neoplasm in all 9 adults followed; 1 found 3 y later (Chan 2001)
Smokers in 16/22 with data (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table)
Cancer identified after neuro onset in 12/23 (52%) (Zekeridou 2022)
Of 3 without cancer on imaging, 2 had a neuroendocrine-predicting antibody profile and 1 was a smoker (Zekeridou 2022)
Authors advise evaluation for occult cancer regardless of neuro diagnosis (Zekeridou 2022)
Not tiered in PNS-Care, so its 2-y rescreening rule is not formally specified (Graus 2021); authors state ANNA-3 fulfils high-risk criteria (Zekeridou 2022)

rationale: Residual specimens: serum 21, CSF 3, both 8 (Zekeridou 2022)
Paired serum/CSF positive in both, except 1 CSF negative by IFA but positive by DACH1 CBA (Zekeridou 2022)
methodNotes: Tissue IFA: nuclear staining of cerebellar Purkinje neurons and renal glomerular podocytes (Zekeridou 2022; Chandna 2024)
Pattern spares Purkinje cytoplasm, granular and enteric neurons; podocyte nuclear staining is not unique (ANNA-2 bound podocyte nuclei in 8/32) (Chan 2001)
Confirm with DACH1 CBA (serum 1:500, CSF 1:2) or western blot; all 145 controls negative (Zekeridou 2022)
Coexisting neural IgGs in 14/30, mostly neuroendocrine-predicting: NIF 3, CRMP5 3, P/Q VGCC 3, ANNA-1 2, SOX1 2, PCA2/MAP1B 1 (Zekeridou 2022)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis or CSF-unique OCB in 4/6 (Zekeridou 2022)

normalPercentText: Brain MRI normal in 10/14 with data (71%) (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table)
typicalFindings: Abnormal: mild atrophy 1; left temporal T2 lesion with biopsy-proven inflammation (limbic encephalitis) 1; diffuse brainstem/cerebellar T2 1; radiation change/metastasis 1 (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table)
Lumbosacral plexus enhancement in polyradiculoneuropathy (1) (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table)
MRI-negative myeloneuropathy reported (Chandna 2024)

otherTests: EMG/NCS: sensory neuronopathy, demyelinating or axonal sensorimotor (poly)radiculoneuropathy (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table; Chan 2001; Chandna 2024)
Autonomic testing abnormal (sweat test, autonomic reflex screen) in small-fiber/autonomic cases (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table)
3 Hz RNS without decrement in 1 (Chandna 2024); LEMS coexisted in 1 (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); cancer in 27/30 (90%) (Zekeridou 2022)
Improvement in 8/11 with data, all after immunotherapy and/or cancer treatment (Zekeridou 2022)
ICI: neuro syndrome appeared or worsened during checkpoint inhibitor therapy in 2 SCLC pts (Zekeridou 2022)
Antibody kept oncologic significance even when an alternative diagnosis emerged: 2 pts with neurodegenerative disease both had cancer (Zekeridou 2022)
SIADH in 3/30 (Zekeridou 2022 suppl table) and in an original pt (Chan 2001)
Rare: 9 pts in 2016–2020 vs 473 ANNA-1-positive pts at Mayo (Zekeridou 2022)
Original description: 11 pts among ~68,000 screened; multifocal neuropathy, ataxia, myelopathy, brainstem/limbic encephalopathy (Chan 2001)

entries.antigen: Septin-7 (cytoskeletal GTP-binding protein; regulates dendritic branching; pre- and postsynaptic localization)

syndromes.syndrome: Subacute encephalopathy with prominent neuropsychiatric features (agitation, apathy, catatonia, disorganized thinking, paranoia, psychosis)
Myelopathy, incl. primary lateral sclerosis-like phenotype
Seizures / nonconvulsive status epilepticus with psychosis

demographics: Septin-7-only cohort (n=15): 8 M, 7 F; age 47–85 y, median 69 (Hinson 2022 Table S2)
cancerScreening: ≥1 concurrent neoplasm in 4/15: breast adenocarcinoma 2, non-Hodgkin lymphoma 1, carcinoid 1, myelodysplastic syndrome 1 (Hinson 2022)
PNS-Care rescreening rule applies only to high-risk antibodies; septin-7 is not tiered (Graus 2021)

rationale: Septin cohort: IFA positive in all 12 CSF and 17/18 sera; 1 pt positive in CSF only (Hinson 2022)
Septin-IgG found in serum + CSF (8), serum only (9), CSF only (6), mostly reflecting sample availability (Hinson 2022)
Median titers (septin-5 + -7 cohort): CSF 1:256, serum 1:15,360 (Hinson 2022)
methodNotes: Tissue IFA 'septin pattern' (diffuse synaptic staining, cerebellar molecular layer, renal glomeruli) plus gastric mucosal and renal interstitial staining in septin-7-positive specimens; confirm by septin-7 CBA (Hinson 2022)
Some epitopes require the septin complex: in 1 pt reactivity depended on septin-7 plus septin-6 or -11 (Gaebler 2026)
Coexisting septin-6/-11 IgG by western blot in 6/7 septin-7 pts tested; IgG1 in all tested, IgG2 in 2 septin-7 pts (Hinson 2022)
Coexisting neurofilament heavy-chain IgG in 1 (Hinson 2022)
Patient IgG binds live hippocampal neuron surfaces, partly colocalizing with PSD-95 (Hinson 2022)

normalPercentText: Non-inflammatory in 4/10 with data (40%), using the authors' definition applied to Table S2 (Hinson 2022)
typicalFindings: Inflammatory (protein >100 mg/dL, lymphocytic pleocytosis, raised IgG synthesis or CSF-exclusive OCB) in 6/10 septin-7 pts (Hinson 2022 Table S2); whole septin cohort 11/15 (Hinson 2022)
Mild protein elevation (42–55 mg/dL) in 3 of the non-inflammatory pts (Hinson 2022 Table S2)
Normal CSF, incl. OCB, at onset and relapse in 1 steroid-responsive psychosis case (Gaebler 2026)

normalPercentText: Normal or nonspecific in 3/9 with data (33%) (Hinson 2022)
typicalFindings: Bilateral hippocampal T2 abnormality 2 (resolved on repeat in 1); generalized cerebral atrophy 2 (Hinson 2022)
Precentral (motor strip) T2 hyperintensity with progressive frontal atrophy in the PLS-like pt (Hinson 2022)
Temporal changes/atrophy in post-HSV-1 cases (Hinson 2022)

otherTests: EEG: triphasic waves in 2, diffuse slowing in 1 (Hinson 2022 Table S2); right temporal nonconvulsive status epilepticus, missed by routine EEG and found on long-term video-EEG, in 1 (Gaebler 2026)
EMG: lumbosacral polyradiculoneuropathy in 1; axonal sensory neuropathy in 1 (Hinson 2022 Table S2)
CSF phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain 1,480 pg/mL in the PLS-like pt (Hinson 2022 Table S2)
pearls: Not tiered in PNS-Care 2021 (Graus 2021); neoplasm in 4/15 (Hinson 2022)
Treatment-responsive: rapid improvement in 4/5 treated; 1 death from steroid-related bowel perforation (Hinson 2022)
The only untreated pt with progressive symptoms had a poor outcome (Hinson 2022)
Psychiatric symptoms prominent in 6/11 encephalopathic pts; 2 had poorly defined neuropsychiatric illness before subacute decline (Hinson 2022)
Antipsychotic-refractory psychosis resolved within 1 wk of IV methylprednisolone and relapsed on taper; antibody identified 5 y after onset (Gaebler 2026)
Followed HSV-1 encephalitis in 2 pts; 1 relapsed 1 wk after acyclovir and largely recovered with steroids + PLEX (Hinson 2022)
Relapsing course in 2 (Hinson 2022)
With coexisting septin-5-IgG the phenotype is ataxia with eye movement disorder instead (Hinson 2022)
Caveat: single-center series (n=15); HSV encephalitis, substance use or prior psychiatric illness coexisted in several pts (Hinson 2022 Table S2)
